query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of Mn with Co in MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials improves mechanical performance by enhancing ductility while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect.
generation.material_initial_state: MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration material in its standard composition.
generation.intervention: Partial substitution of Mn with Co at a substitution level of up to 10 atomic percent.
generation.conditions: Room temperature to cryogenic temperatures, under conditions relevant to magnetic refrigeration applications.
generation.structural_mediator: Modification of the crystal lattice and electronic structure due to Co substitution.
generation.mechanism: Co substitution alters the bonding characteristics and reduces brittleness by introducing more metallic bonding character, while maintaining the magnetic ordering necessary for a large magnetocaloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical performance, specifically increased ductility, without significant reduction in the magnetocaloric effect (less than 5% reduction in the isothermal entropy change relative to the baseline).
generation.baseline: Mechanical performance and magnetocaloric effect of the unmodified MnNiSi-based material.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold for Co substitution levels up to 10 atomic percent. Beyond this level, the magnetocaloric effect may degrade significantly.
generation.uncertainty: The exact level of Co substitution that optimally balances mechanical performance and magnetocaloric effect is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize MnNiSi-based materials with varying levels of Co substitution (e.g., 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%) and measure their mechanical properties (e.g., ductility, fracture toughness) and magnetocaloric effect (e.g., isothermal entropy change).
measurements: Isothermal entropy change (ΔS) under an applied magnetic field
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Co substitution at any level up to 10 atomic percent does not improve mechanical performance or results in a reduction of the magnetocaloric effect by more than 5%, the hypothesis is falsified.
